insight.title: Why Copying Winners Makes You Lose
insight.subtitle: How following industry leaders causes you to inherit their mistakes

sections.text: We watch a market leader and assume their newest move is genius. We rush to mirror it. Usually, they are just experimenting, and now you are both lost on the same map.

This is "Strategic Mimicry." We incorrectly believe that because a company is bigger, they are more certain. But size often masks confusion. Copying them doesn't lower your risk; it just removes your edge.
Real strategy is found in the gaps others leave behind. If your roadmap is a mirror of someone else’s, you aren’t building a business—you are simply building a shadow of one.
Try this today: When you think about a competitor today, ask if you actually want their specific problems.
You cannot win the race if you are only following someone else's footprints.

news.title: US Iran War: No air strikes in UAE for first time, but Hormuz still choked
news.description: The UAE has reported its first day without air strikes since the conflict started on February 28. No missiles or drones were detected from Iran. However, the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

news.title: Macro buffers to help India tide over Gulf crisis: World Bank
news.description: India's economic growth for FY27 is projected at 6.6 percent. The World Bank notes potential risks from the Gulf conflict impacting global energy prices. However, India's economy is strong, supported by reserves and low inflation. Growth is expected to average 7.1 percent from FY28 to FY29. Boosting private sector growth is key for job creation and achieving Viksit Bharat.

news.title: 'Rate action unlikely in FY27; if any, it could be a rise,' say economists
news.description: Indian markets expect a prolonged pause in policy rates. Economists foresee no immediate tightening as higher global energy prices have a limited impact. The Reserve Bank of India is likely to maintain rates through FY27. While most anticipate a pause, a rate hike is considered more probable than a cut if the Iran conflict persists and affects growth.

news.title: From bottles to cosmetics: How plastics are impacting human health
news.description: Research has shown that chemicals in everyday plastics are driving a global health crisis, linked to hundreds of thousands of deaths and diseases from heart conditions to cancer.

news.description: The US Postal Service said Thursday it would temporarily suspend payments to an employee pension plan to free up cash amid a financial crisis.

news.title: Ceasefire Challenges: Israel, Lebanon, and Global Tensions
news.description: The ongoing conflict between Israel and Lebanon escalates as Israel seeks direct talks with Beirut amid a U.S.-Iran ceasefire jeopardized by continuous tensions. Iran remains defiant, and Pakistan steps in as a mediator. Lebanon declares a day of mourning after devastating attacks, while Iran and the U.S. both claim victory.
